concept.shortExplanation: Once meaning is geometry, comparing two words becomes a distance calculation. Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their length, which is why it is the default choice — it asks whether two words point the same way, not how emphatic they are. Euclidean distance answers a different question and will rank things differently. Every number in this chapter is computed live from real embeddings.
concept.ahaMoment: Retrieval, search, recommendation and RAG are all this one operation at scale: embed everything once, then answer queries by finding the nearest angle. The whole retrieval industry is a dot product with good indexing.

modelRequirement.loadFailureMessage: The embedding model could not be downloaded. Check your connection and retry — once cached, this chapter runs fully offline.

levels.title: Rank by Similarity
levels.instructions: Drag the words into order, nearest to the anchor word at the top. Your ordering is compared against the real cosine ranking using rank correlation.

levels.title: Odd One Out
levels.instructions: One word in each set sits furthest from the others in embedding space. Find it. The outlier is determined live by mean pairwise cosine similarity, not by a stored answer.

levels.title: Cosine vs Euclidean
levels.instructions: Bring your own words. Build a set of five, then predict which pairs the two metrics will disagree about. The heatmap recomputes live under both metrics as you type.
